{{Short description|Equality operator on partial functions}}
In [[mathematics]], '''Kleene equality''',<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/Kleene+equality|title=Kleene equality in nLab|website=ncatlab.org}}</ref> or '''strong equality''', (<math>\simeq</math>) is an equality operator on [[partial functions]], that states that on a given argument either both functions are undefined, or both are defined and their values on that arguments are equal.

For example, if we have partial functions <math>f</math> and <math>g</math>, <math>f \simeq g</math> means that for every <math>x</math>:{{sfn|Cutland|1980|p=3}}
* <math>f(x)</math> and <math>g(x)</math> are both defined and <math>f(x) = g(x)</math>
* or <math>f(x)</math> and <math>g(x)</math> are both undefined.

Some authors<ref name="Farmer">{{cite journal
|title=	A Set Theory with Support for Partial Functions
|author1=Farmer, William M.
|author2=Guttman, Joshua D. 
|journal= Studia Logica|volume= 66
|issue = 1
|date=2000
|pages=59–78
|jstor=20016214
|url = http://www.jstor.org/stable/20016214
}}
</ref> are using "quasi-equality", which is defined like this:
<math>
(y_1 \sim y_2):\Leftrightarrow((y_1\downarrow \lor y_2\downarrow)\longrightarrow y_1=y_2),
</math>
where the down arrow means that the term on the left side of it is defined.
Then it becomes possible to define the strong equality in the following way:
<math>
(f \simeq g):\Leftrightarrow (\forall x. (f(x)\sim g(x))).
</math>
